title: Bank Exam Preparation for 2027: A Beginner's Plan
excerpt: Start your bank exam preparation for 2027 with a beginner-friendly study plan covering syllabus, Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, English, mock tests, and time management.
content:
Bank Exam Preparation for 2027: A Beginner's Plan

Preparing for bank exams in 2027 requires a clear study plan, strong fundamentals, regular practice, and effective time management. For beginners, understanding the syllabus and choosing the right preparation strategy are important first steps. GICE Academy offers banking exam coaching with experienced subject experts, comprehensive study materials, weekly full-length mock tests, personalised mentorship, and doubt-solving support to help aspirants prepare systematically for examinations such as IBPS PO, IBPS Clerk, SBI PO, SBI Clerk, IBPS RRB, and RBI recruitment exams.


With GICE Academy, banking aspirants can focus on:


  1. Concept-Based Learning: Build a strong foundation in Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning Ability, and English Language.
  2. Structured Study Planning: Follow a time-bound preparation routine with regular revision.
  3. Exam-Oriented Practice: Practise questions using pattern-based question banks and previous-year papers.
  4. Mock Test Preparation: Evaluate performance through regular full-length mock tests.
  5. Performance Improvement: Identify weak areas, review mistakes, and improve speed and accuracy.
  6. Personalised Mentorship: Get guidance and doubt-solving support throughout your preparation.
  7. Flexible Learning: Explore suitable class timings and preparation options according to your schedule.

﻿

Explore GICE Academy’s Banking Coaching Programme to learn more about its preparation support and available learning options. Combine structured guidance with consistent self-study and regular practice to develop an effective approach to competitive banking examinations.

In this guide, you will learn how to understand bank exam patterns and eligibility, select important syllabus topics, choose suitable books and study materials, create a realistic timetable, improve speed and accuracy, and analyse mock tests. Whether you are starting from zero or strengthening your existing preparation, this beginner-friendly plan will help you organise your bank exam preparation for 2027.

A beginner does not need to master every subject before starting bank exam preparation. You need a target and a repeatable routine. A manageable plan, syllabus awareness, and regular practice matter more than collecting books and apps. You can begin before a recruitment notice appears, even if official 2027 dates are not available here.

First, learn how the exams differ and choose a realistic target. Then build core skills and track your progress with focused practice. A sectional test is a timed set of questions from one exam section, taken separately from a full mock test. You can start now without knowing every topic or having a perfect study plan. This guide offers a practical route from understanding the exams to planning daily study, beginning with their different formats.

Key Takeaways

  1. Choose one main exam target before buying study materials.
  2. Use the current official syllabus to set your starting point.
  3. Learn concepts before trying to race through questions.
  4. Review mistakes to see what needs more practice.
  5. Keep a steady routine that fits your daily responsibilities.

What should you know about bank exam patterns and eligibility?

A typical bank recruitment process starts with a timed prelims paper, but the exact stages depend on the exam. Use the pattern as a guide, not a promise: recruitment rules and exam pattern details can change by year. Check the current official IBPS, SBI, or RBI notification for stages, eligibility, and marking rules.

What do prelims and mains test?

One common PO and clerk prelims structure has 100 questions across English, quantitative aptitude, and reasoning. The total time is 60 minutes, with 20 minutes for each section.

One common mains pattern adds reasoning and computer aptitude, awareness, English, data analysis and interpretation, and a descriptive English task. Prelims mainly test speed, while mains usually ask for deeper analysis and broader awareness.

PO recruitment includes an interview stage. Clerk recruitment generally does not, though each notice sets the final process.

Is a bank PO very difficult?

A bank PO exam can be challenging because many candidates compete, questions are timed, and the starting level varies. If math or English feels rusty, that does not predict your final result. It shows where to begin.

Build accuracy with untimed practice before pushing for speed. Then add timed questions and learn to leave a question that is taking too long.

Which bank exam is easy to pass?

No bank exam is easy for everyone. Clerk and RRB Office Assistant roles may suit candidates who prefer recruitment without an interview, but the written exam still takes steady preparation.

Compare the role, location, eligibility, language needs, and exam stages before choosing. A familiar regional language or stronger fit with the syllabus may make one exam more practical for you.

What is the salary of a bank PO?

In salary figures listed for 2026, basic PO pay was ₹36,000. Gross monthly pay ranged from ₹62,000-₹75,000 for IBPS PO and ₹65,000-₹77,000 for SBI PO.

These 2026 figures are historical context, not a promise for 2027. Allowances and work location affect gross pay, and the current recruitment notice or bank details set the terms.

Can you prepare for banking after 12th?

Yes. After 12th grade, you can build math, reading, and reasoning skills while learning about bank roles. Major PO and clerk recruitment generally requires graduation, though rules can vary.

Check the official notice for the exam you want, including its age, degree, and language requirements. Use its syllabus to decide what to study first.

What should you study first as a beginner?

If the syllabus looks like a long list, divide it into four familiar areas and mark what you already know. Start with basic concepts, then try questions without a timer. Your first goal is to understand each topic, not to finish the syllabus quickly.

Download the syllabus from the official recruitment site for your chosen exam. Sections can vary, so do not assume every bank exam tests the same subjects.

How to start banking preparation from zero level

How to start banking preparation from zero level means building useful concepts and study habits before chasing speed. Begin with these steps:


  1. Map the official syllabus and mark familiar topics.
  2. Diagnose weak areas with a few basic questions.
  3. Learn one topic at a time before moving ahead.
  4. Keep short notes for rules, errors, and key facts.
  5. Solve topic-level questions after each lesson.


Quantitative aptitude covers number skills and data work. Reasoning uses patterns and logic, while English language builds reading and grammar skills. General awareness may include current affairs and banking news.

Which topics belong on your first syllabus checklist?

For quantitative aptitude, a useful sequence is number system, simplification, percentages, profit and loss, interest, ratio and proportion, time and work, speed and distance, averages, then data interpretation.

For reasoning, start with linear and circular seating, puzzles, syllogism, inequality, blood relations, direction sense, coding-decoding, and number series. Read English regularly and practice comprehension. Add general awareness based on your exam's syllabus.

Which books and study materials are worth starting with?

Keep your bank exam preparation books and online tools to a small set. R.S. Aggarwal is one option for quantitative aptitude and reasoning practice. Use a newspaper or trusted current-affairs compilation for news.

Choose one source for concepts and another for questions, rather than switching between many books. Check that online material matches the current notification; old lessons may miss changed topics or rules.

Once your subjects are mapped, set a realistic sequence and timeframe for learning them.

How to Plan Bank Exam Preparation for 2027

A useful 2027 plan begins with the exam date when it is announced, not a guessed recruitment calendar. Until then, work from your target exam and current level. Stay flexible because each notice sets its own dates and details.

SBI PO, IBPS PO, SBI Clerk, IBPS Clerk, and RRB exams share roughly 80-90% syllabus overlap. Still, choose one primary target and, if useful, one closely related backup. Count backward from the official exam date once it appears.

Build concepts first, then add timed practice

Start by learning concepts and solving topic-level questions. When the basics feel steady, add sectional tests and mains-level topics, including awareness and data analysis.

In the final stage, give more time to mocks, revision, and current affairs. Do not wait for prelims results before starting mains awareness work; begin it alongside prelims preparation.

A sample 90-day plan can use one month for foundations, one for practice, and one for revision and mocks. Treat that as a planning example, not a guarantee.

Work backward from the notification, not an assumed calendar

If you study 2-3 hours each day, around 5-6 months may be a useful planning estimate. Your starting skills and the exam date can shorten or extend that time.

With less time, focus on core gaps and high-value practice rather than trying to cover every resource. With more time, build concepts at a calmer pace and revisit weak areas.

Once the stages are set, improve performance through deliberate practice and feedback.

How can you improve speed, accuracy and current affairs?

A higher mock score helps only when you can explain which decisions improved it. Use each mock test to find a skill or choice to work on. One score is a clue, not a final judgment. Never guess blindly when the notification applies negative marking.

Many major bank exams use 0.25-mark negative marking for wrong answers, but the current notification sets the rule. Leave a question when you cannot narrow the choices with reason.

Build speed through focused practice. Mental calculations and data interpretation can help with quantitative aptitude. In reasoning, choose puzzles carefully and move on if one set consumes too much time.

Regular reading and comprehension practice support English. For general awareness, follow banking and financial news, RBI updates, government schemes, and economic developments.

Mains current-affairs preparation commonly focuses on the 5-6 months just before the exam. Keep a current-affairs log and review it weekly, instead of cramming at the end.


After each mock, check these points:

  1. How many questions did you attempt?
  2. How accurate were your answers?
  3. How much time did each question take?
  4. Which questions did you skip, and why?
  5. Which error type keeps returning?


Use the results to choose your next practice task, not to judge your ability. Keep these checks in a routine you can sustain alongside other responsibilities.

Can you prepare for banking exams through self-study?

A full-time coaching schedule is not necessary if you can protect consistent study blocks each week. Self-study can work with official notifications, a steady set of books, previous-year papers, and regular mocks. For many beginners, 2-3 focused hours a day is a practical starting point.

A 5-6-month preparation period is an example, not a rule. Your baseline, weekly time, and exam date decide how much preparation you need.

A self-study timetable for bank exam preparation

Use this self-study time table for bank exam preparation as a sample week. Move sessions to fit work, college, travel, or family duties.


  1. Practice quantitative aptitude questions.
  2. Work on reasoning questions and puzzles.
  3. Read English and answer comprehension questions.
  4. Review current affairs and banking news.
  5. Try mixed practice across the subjects you have studied.
  6. Take one full mock, then set aside a separate session to review it.


Keep each session focused on one task. If a work shift or class disrupts the week, resume with the next planned block instead of doubling your workload.

How to choose apps, online material or coaching

Coaching is optional. It may help if you need structure, feedback, or a teacher to explain doubts, but you can build those habits through planned self-study.

When choosing a bank exam preparation app for 2026, check whether its syllabus, current affairs, and mock patterns match the 2027 recruitment cycle. An old app label does not prove its content is current.

The best free app for bank exam preparation should give accurate explanations, current material, and a way to track practice. Try its sample questions before relying on it.

Choose one routine and resource set, then follow them long enough to judge your progress.

Conclusion

The best first step is small enough to take today and clear enough to repeat tomorrow. Steady preparation, focused practice, and mistake review matter more than changing resources each week.

Find the official notification or syllabus for your chosen exam. Mark the first three topics you need to learn, then set your first study block and begin with one topic.

title: SSC CGL Salary 2026: In-Hand Pay, Posts and Perks
excerpt: SSC CGL Salary 2026: Check post-wise pay levels, estimated in-hand salary by city, DA, HRA, allowances, deductions, job profiles, perks and career growth.
content:
SSC CGL Salary 2026: In-Hand Pay, Posts and Perks

Planning a government career involves understanding both the SSC CGL selection process and the salary, allowances, and career opportunities associated with different posts. GICE Academy supports SSC CGL aspirants with structured preparation, subject guidance, practice questions, mock tests, and performance analysis. With a focused study plan, candidates can strengthen their concepts, improve speed and accuracy, and prepare systematically for the examination.


With GICE Academy, SSC CGL aspirants can focus on:


  1. Structured SSC CGL Preparation: Follow a planned approach to cover the examination syllabus.
  2. Subject-Wise Guidance: Strengthen Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, English, and General Awareness.
  3. Mock Tests and Practice: Build exam readiness through sectional and full-length tests.
  4. Performance Analysis: Identify weak areas, review mistakes, and improve accuracy.
  5. Revision and Time Management: Practise regularly to improve speed and use exam time effectively.
  6. Tier-I and Tier-II Preparation: Build a preparation strategy that considers both stages of the examination.
  7. Career and Post Awareness: Understand different SSC CGL posts, pay levels, job responsibilities, allowances, and promotion opportunities.


Along with exam preparation, knowing the salary structure can help aspirants compare government posts and make informed career choices. Explore GICE Academy’s SSC CGL coaching programme to learn more about its preparation approach.

In this guide, we explain SSC CGL Salary 2026, including estimated in-hand salary, post-wise pay levels, allowances, perks, deductions, job profiles, and career progression. You will also learn why actual take-home pay can vary depending on the post, posting location, applicable allowances, and deductions.

There is no single SSC CGL take-home figure for every selected candidate. A candidate comparing government careers needs to look beyond the pay level and ask what will reach a bank account each month.

Gross salary means basic pay plus applicable allowances before deductions are taken. The advertised role, pay level, posting city, allowances and deductions all shape the final amount. Pay-matrix figures show a salary range, not a guaranteed monthly deposit.

The figures below help candidates compare likely earnings before choosing a post. They also separate gross pay from in-hand salary, the amount credited after deductions. Duties and service benefits matter too, since a higher estimate may come with work or posting conditions that do not suit every candidate.

Key Takeaways

  1. Estimated in-hand pay varies by post, pay level and city.
  2. A pay scale shows a range, not a new recruit’s take-home pay.
  3. Allowances raise gross salary, while deductions lower the amount deposited.
  4. Compare duties, posting and career path alongside monthly pay.
  5. Check the current SSC notice and allowance rules before setting preferences.

The quick estimate spans about ₹40,000 to ₹81,000 per month. These are estimates, not a universal payslip.

SSC CGL Salary: What Can You Earn in 2026?

Estimated SSC CGL salary in-hand pay ranges from about ₹40,000 to ₹81,000 per month. That span is a practical guide, not a promise for every new employee.

The pay scale’s maximum is not an entry-level monthly salary. Starting basic pay depends on the post’s pay level, while city and allowances affect gross salary. Deductions then change the amount credited to your account.

The latest SSC notice represented here covers Levels 4 through 7. Each level has a starting basic pay and a higher ceiling reached through pay progression. A new recruit does not start at that ceiling.

Your SSC CGL salary per month starting amount may differ from another candidate’s, even at the same level. The posting city can change housing and travel allowances, while deductions affect in-hand salary. Use the range to frame expectations, then compare the specific post and city.

Salary research is separate from exam preparation. “SSC CGL salary syllabus” is not an official exam component; the syllabus covers the subjects and skills tested. Keep pay questions apart from checking the cgl exam syllabus and exam notices.

The cgl salary 2026 range comes from the pay components and levels behind each role. The next step is seeing how basic pay and allowances combine.

How Is SSC CGL Pay Structured?

On a monthly payslip, basic pay is one line, while gross salary adds applicable allowances. Basic pay is the starting point, not the full amount earned.

Basic pay plus applicable allowances equals gross salary; deductions then reduce the in-hand amount. The 7th Pay Commission sets pay levels and pay scales for the covered roles.

These pay levels show the starting basic pay and the possible scale within each level. Grade pay appears in the older structure, but the 7th Pay Commission uses the pay matrix to set basic pay.

A scale ceiling is not a promise of starting salary. Your pay can rise within the level over time, while allowances depend on rules and posting details. Your salary slip records the actual earnings and deductions for that month.

The next practical step is matching each pay level to the posts assigned to it.

Which SSC CGL Posts Belong to Each Pay Level?

One candidate may prefer a desk-based assistant role, while another chooses an inspector post. The pay level sets the band, so the title alone does not set starting pay.

Among the levels covered here, Level 4 has the lowest starting basic pay, ₹25,500. The posts below are examples, and candidates should check the notice for the exact post list.

Level 7 posts and starting pay

Level 7 starts at ₹44,900 basic pay. Examples include Assistant Section Officer and Inspector of Income Tax, a post under the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT).

Other examples include Inspector (Central Excise) under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Inspector (Preventive Officer), and Inspector (Examiner). The list also includes Assistant Enforcement Officer in the Directorate of Enforcement, Sub-Inspector in the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Inspector Posts and Inspector in the Central Bureau of Narcotics.

The Inspector of Income Tax is the relevant SSC CGL post title here. “Income Tax Officer” is not the listed title, so do not treat the two names as interchangeable.

Level 6 posts and starting pay

Level 6 starts at ₹35,400 basic pay. Examples include Executive Assistant, Research Assistant at the National Human Rights Commission, and Divisional Accountant in Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C&AG) offices.

This level also includes Sub-Inspector in the National Investigation Agency (NIA), Sub-Inspector or Junior Intelligence Officer in the Narcotics Control Bureau, and Junior Statistical Officer (JSO). The role name gives a clue to the work, but the assigned department and post conditions matter too.

Level 5 posts and starting pay

Level 5 starts at ₹29,200 basic pay. Auditor roles include posts in C&AG offices, and the level also has Accountant and Junior Accountant roles.

These posts focus on accounts and records. Their starting basic pay is higher than Level 4 and lower than Levels 6 and 7. The exact department and duties can differ by vacancy.

Level 4 posts and starting pay

Level 4 starts at ₹25,500 basic pay. Examples include Postal Assistant or Sorting Assistant, Senior Secretariat Assistant or Upper Division Clerk, and Senior Administrative Assistant.

Tax Assistant and Sub-Inspector in the Central Bureau of Narcotics are also listed at Level 4. Postal Assistant or Sorting Assistant is a Level 4 role with a starting basic pay of ₹25,500, not ₹29,200.

These starting amounts are tied to pay levels, while gross salary changes with allowances. City and allowance rules are the next factors to compare.

How Does Posting City Change Gross Salary?

Two employees at the same pay level can receive different gross salary because their city categories differ. Housing allowance is a key reason for the gap.

The city category affects House Rent Allowance (HRA), so these gross figures are estimates, not official take-home slips. X cities show the highest illustrative gross amount in each level below.

The figures compare estimated gross monthly pay across city classes. They do not show the net amount deposited after deductions, and the actual posting details can change the calculation.

TA eligibility and the location of a posting can also cause variation. HRA and other applicable allowances help explain why employees with the same basic pay may see different gross amounts.

Gross salary is not the amount deposited after deductions. The next comparison shows estimated in-hand pay.

What Is the SSC CGL In-Hand Salary After Deductions?

In-hand salary is gross salary less deductions. It is the amount credited to your bank account after the monthly pay calculation.

Actual in-hand pay varies by pay level, city, deductions and applicable rules. The estimates below show a practical comparison, not a fixed amount for every employee.

The exact take-home amount depends on the employee’s earnings and deductions. A salary slip is the monthly record of those earnings and deductions, including basic pay, allowances and recoveries.

Deductions can include National Pension System (NPS), Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme (CGEGIS), and other applicable recoveries. Income tax depends on taxable income and the rules that apply to the employee.

Common deduction categories include:


  1. NPS contributions
  2. CGHS contributions
  3. CGEGIS contributions
  4. Other applicable recoveries

﻿

Do not apply one universal deduction total to every salary estimate. Tax, department-specific recoveries and other individual details can change the amount that reaches your account.

Allowances build gross salary before these deductions are taken. Their rules explain why employees at one pay level can have different earnings.

Which Allowances and Perks Add to SSC CGL Pay?

Allowances explain why the same basic pay can produce different gross pay. They depend on rules and location, rather than adding the same amount for every employee.

The DA figure used here is 58% of basic pay as of March 20, 2026. Allowance rates can change, so do not call this figure current later in 2026 without checking for a newer order.

Dearness Allowance and cost-of-living changes

Dearness Allowance (DA) helps adjust pay for changes in the cost of living. The government can revise it through orders, so a dated rate should not be treated as permanent.

DA is calculated as a share of basic pay. A change in the rate can affect gross salary and can also trigger a change in HRA under the set formula.

HRA and city categories

House Rent Allowance helps with housing costs. Under the HRA trigger formula, rates are 27% for X cities, 18% for Y cities and 9% for Z cities once DA exceeds 50%.

HRA rates depend on the city category and the applicable rule. Do not assume that every employee gets an identical rent allowance, or that an allowance always matches actual rent paid.

Transport, medical and post-specific benefits

For Pay Levels 3 through 8, Transport Allowance (TA) is ₹3,600 plus DA in higher Transport Allowance cities. In other locations, it is ₹1,800 plus DA.

Medical support and other central government service benefits depend on the rules that apply to the employee. A sensitive organization may provide a special security allowance where applicable, but no single amount applies to every post.

An allowance or reimbursement may have conditions and may not be an automatic cash benefit. Once you understand what can raise pay, the nature of each post becomes the next question.

What Do SSC CGL Roles Involve, and Which Are Field Posts?

A desk-based file assignment differs from an inspection or inquiry. The job profile matters alongside pay, because field duties can shape a working day.

Assistant, auditor and accountant roles are generally administrative or records-focused, while some inspector and investigation posts include field work. Stress depends on duties, workload and posting, so no single rating fits every department.

Desk-based administration and accounts

Assistant Section Officer (ASO) work is generally administrative. An assistant may help manage files and office tasks, while auditor and accountant roles handle bills, expenditure records and related financial work.

These roles can involve regular deadlines and detailed records. The day-to-day mix depends on the department and assignment, so a desk-based post does not mean every workday looks the same.

Income Tax Inspectors handle tax-related assessment and matters involving tax deducted at source (TDS) or refunds. Their work may combine office tasks with contact tied to the post.

Inspection and investigative work

Central Excise Inspectors work to prevent duty evasion and may support raid operations. Preventive Officer duties can involve work beyond an office, based on the specific posting.

Assistant Enforcement Officers work on financial-crime investigations, including money laundering and forgery. CBI and NIA Sub-Inspectors take part in inquiries and investigations.

These examples show why “field post” is not a full description of a role. The duties and workload vary by organization, assignment and location.

Statistical and data-focused roles

JSOs and Statistical Investigators support data collection, tabulation and reports. The work is built around information and analysis, though specific tasks depend on the post.

Uniformed posts do not share one salary rate. CBI Sub-Inspector is Level 7, while NIA Sub-Inspector is Level 6, so use the pay-level and city estimates above.

Role stress varies with duties, workload and posting. There is no single rating that applies to every department or candidate. Salary can also change over time through increments and promotion.

How Can SSC CGL Salary Change After Five or Ten Years?

Salary generally progresses, but there is no single five- or ten-year figure for every post. Each career path differs by cadre, promotion timing and pay rules.

A reliable universal SSC CGL salary after 5 years or after 10 years cannot be calculated from a post title alone. Allowances and promotion timing can change before either point.

Increment and DA changes

Annual increments can raise basic pay within the pay matrix. DA revisions can also change gross salary, while future allowance orders may differ from today’s rates.

The amount depends on the employee’s pay progression and the rules in force at the time. A current estimate cannot stand in for a future payslip.

Promotion and post-specific progression

Promotion routes, seniority and departmental exams may affect how quickly a candidate moves to another role or pay level. Each cadre has its own eligibility and timing.


To estimate an individual path, check these details in order:

  1. Confirm the post and cadre.
  2. Check the applicable increment and pay-matrix rules.
  3. Verify promotion routes and eligibility.
  4. Use the DA and city rates in force at that future date.


An assistant section role and an inspector role may have different progression rules. Your department’s service rules give the relevant path, rather than a single estimate for all SSC CGL posts.

Long-term pay is only one part of a government career. Retirement and other service benefits also matter when you compare a role.

Do SSC CGL Employees Get Pension or an Official Car?

NPS-linked retirement benefits apply, while a car is not established as a universal benefit. Neither benefit should be assumed in the same way for every post.

NPS is a retirement savings scheme, not a guaranteed old-style pension. Employees and the government make monthly contributions under the scheme.

Medical, leave and other central service benefits depend on the applicable rules. CGHS and CGEGIS are among the service schemes named for employees, but eligibility and terms should be checked for the post.

An official or personal car is not a standard promise for every SSC CGL employee. Any vehicle access depends on the department and duties, so do not count it as a universal perk.


Check these benefit categories in the relevant service rules:

  1. NPS retirement savings
  2. Health coverage
  3. Leave
  4. Post-specific allowances


These rules help separate a confirmed service benefit from an assumption about a particular role. With monthly pay and service terms in view, candidates can compare posts against their own priorities.

How Should You Compare SSC CGL Posts Before Filling Preferences?

A candidate may accept a higher-paying field role, while another may prefer a desk-based job that better fits personal priorities. Fit can matter more than a small estimated pay gap.

Compare the work and posting as well as the pay level before ranking posts. Gender does not change the salary structure described here, and no role should be assigned a gender-based preference.


Use these four points to weigh the options:

  1. Starting pay level for the listed post
  2. Desk-based duties versus field work
  3. Likely posting location and transfers
  4. Career progression within the post and cadre

﻿

SSC CGL is not formally called “mini IAS.” The exam recruits for Group B and Group C posts, while the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) is a separate service.

Pay estimates cannot tell you whether a role’s duties or transfers will suit you. A modest difference in monthly pay may matter less than the work setting you want for several years.

Compare official post details rather than relying on a nickname or general claim. The next check is why published salary figures can disagree.

Why Do SSC CGL Salary Figures Differ?

Different assumptions, rather than one universal payslip, often explain conflicting figures. Small rule changes matter when an estimate combines pay, allowances and deductions.

City class, TA eligibility, deductions, post and the DA calculation date can all change an estimate. A figure without those details may not match your own pay.

There is also conflicting information about whether Level 8 Assistant Audit Officer or Assistant Accounts Officer roles belong in the current list. The latest notice represented here covers Levels 4 through 7.

Do not include Level 8 or claim an updated allowance rate without checking the relevant current SSC notification and government orders. Verify the post list and pay rules for your choice before relying on an estimate.

That check gives you a sound basis for judging an offer and finalizing preferences.

Conclusion

No single SSC CGL salary number applies to every post and location. Starting pay depends on the listed post, while estimated in-hand pay changes with the city and deductions.

Compare the pay level with the duties and likely posting before choosing a role. A higher estimate may not outweigh work conditions that do not fit your needs.

Check the current SSC notification and applicable allowance orders for your chosen post. Verify the current post list and pay rules for your preferred role before finalizing post preferences.

content:
1) भारत के तेजस्विन शंकर ने बर्मिंघम में चल रहे राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2022 में पुरुषों की ऊंची कूद के फाइनल में 2.22 मीटर के साथ कांस्य पदक जीता।

➨23 वर्षीय ने पुरुषों की ऊंची कूद स्पर्धा में देश का पहला एथलेटिक्स पदक जीता।

2) एयू स्मॉल फाइनेंस बैंक ने एक अभिनव क्रेडिट कार्ड उत्पाद लॉन्च किया है जो क्रेडिट कार्ड परिदृश्य में क्रांतिकारी बदलाव लाता है।

3) सेबी ने हाइब्रिड प्रतिभूतियों पर एक सलाहकार समिति का गठन किया है, जो ऐसे उपकरणों के विकास को बढ़ावा देने के लिए सिफारिशें करेगी, जिसमें जारी करने में आसानी और घरेलू और वैश्विक पूंजी को आकर्षित करने पर ध्यान केंद्रित करने वाले उपाय शामिल हैं।

➠➠भारतीय प्रतिभूति और विनिमय बोर्ड (सेबी) भारत सरकार के वित्त मंत्रालय के अधिकार क्षेत्र में भारत में प्रतिभूतियों और कमोडिटी बाजार के लिए नियामक निकाय है। यह 12 अप्रैल 1988 को स्थापित किया गया था और सेबी अधिनियम, 1992 के माध्यम से 30 जनवरी 1992 को वैधानिक शक्तियां प्रदान की गईं।

4) चेन्नई स्थित ड्रोन स्टार्ट-अप गरुड़ एयरोस्पेस ने मलेशिया में अपना पहला एयरोस्पेस प्लांट स्थापित करने के लिए मलेशियाई ड्रोन सॉल्यूशन कंपनी, HiiLSE Global SdnBhd (HiiLSE ड्रोन) के साथ भागीदारी की है।

5) केंद्र ने खुफिया एजेंसी की रिसर्च एंड एनालिसिस विंग (रॉ) के सचिव के रूप में सामंत कुमार गोयल का अनुबंध एक और साल के लिए बढ़ा दिया था।

➨मंत्रिमंडल की नियुक्ति समिति ने भी तपन कुमार डेका को इंटेलिजेंस ब्यूरो (आईबी) के अगले निदेशक के रूप में नियुक्त करने की पुष्टि की।

title: Current Affairs for 14th August 2022 – English
content:
1) Justice Uday Umesh Lalit has been appointed the 49th Chief Justice of India (CJI) after President Droupadi Murmu signed his warrant of appointment.

➨Justice Lalit will assume charge on August 27, a day after Justice N.V. Ramana demits office as the CJI.

2) Eminent exponent of Assam’s classical Sattriya dance and Sangeet Natak Akademi awardee Garima Hazarika died due to old age ailments. She was 83.

3) The Athletics Federation of India (AFI) celebrated August 7 as National Javelin Day across the country to commemorate one of the greatest moments in the country’s sporting history, Neeraj Chopra’s Olympic gold medal.

4) Power Grid Corporation of India Limited has appointed Pramod Kumar as chief financial officer (CFO) of the company.

5) Chess prodigy V Pranav became India’s 75th Grandmaster by winning a tournament in Romania.

➨The Chennai-based Pranav won the Limpedea Open in Baia Mare, Romania to secure his third and final GM norm and attain the Grandmaster title

6) Veteran Marathi actor Pradeep Patwardhan, passed away.

➨He was known for his performance in films such as “Chashme Bahaddar”, “Ek Shodh” and “Mee Shivajiraje Bhosale Boltoy”

7) The Indian Army in collaboration with the Drone Federation of India has launched the ‘Him Drone-a-thon’ programme.

8) Tibetan spiritual leader Dalai Lama was honoured with the ‘dPal rNgam Duston’ award — the highest civilian honour of Ladakh — for his immense contribution to humanity, especially towards the union territory.

9) Google has launched an online project named ‘India Ki Udaan’, to celebrate India’s 75-years journey of independence.

➨Under this project, Google will put up an online exhibition of informative content to showcase India’s contribution and journey in the last 75 years.

10) Grandmaster and five-time World Champion Viswanathan Anand has been elected as the deputy president of FIDE, the international chess body.

➨ Russian and incumbent president Arkady Dvorkovich was successfully re-elected as FIDE President.

11) The 13th edition of Ex Vajra Prahar 2022 exercise between the special forces of India and the US began in Himachal Pradesh’s Bakloh to improve inter-operability between these special forces of both the countries.

12) Maharashtra Governor Shri Bhagat Singh Koshyari inaugurated the 22nd ‘Bharat Rang Mahotsav’ at Rabindra Natya Mandir in Mumbai.

title: SBI PO Online Form 2022 Notification Out
content:
The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) has released the IBPS PO 2026 Notification (CRP PO/MTXVI) on 30th June 2026, announcing 6,715 vacancies for Probationary Officer and Management Trainee posts across 11 participating public sector banks. This is one of the highest vacancy counts in recent years, roughly 1,507 more posts than the previous cycle, making 2026 an excellent year for banking aspirants to attempt this

exam.

Online applications for IBPS PO recruitment 2026 opened on 1st July 2026 and will close on 21st July 2026. This guide walks you through every detail you need: vacancy break-up, eligibility, the revised exam pattern, salary structure, syllabus, and a complete preparation roadmap so you can apply with confidence and prepare with a clear plan.

What is IBPS PO?

IBPS PO refers to the Common Recruitment Process for Probationary Officers conducted by the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection to fill officer-level vacancies in public sector banks. Running since 2011, this is the 16th edition of the exam, officially referred to as CRP PO/MT-XVI. Selected candidates begin their banking careers as probationary officers or management trainees before being confirmed as assistant managers after a probation period.

IBPS itself was established in 1984 on the mandate of the Reserve Bank of India, evolving from the earlier Personnel Selection Services set up in 1975. Today, it conducts common recruitment for probationary officers, clerks, Specialist Officers, and Regional Rural Bank staff, making it the single largest recruiter into India’s public banking sector.


For the latest IBPS PO updates and expert preparation support, keep following our website regularly.

Why IBPS PO is One of India’s Most Preferred Banking Jobs

Lakhs of graduates attempt the IBPS PO exam every year, and for good reason. Here is what makes this role so sought-after:

● Officer-Level Entry: You start your banking career directly as an officer, not a clerk, with faster

growth into managerial roles.

● Job Security: Public sector bank jobs offer strong stability and a defined pension/retirement

framework.

● Attractive Pay & Perks: A competitive starting salary combined with DA, HRA, and multiple

allowances.

● Nationwide Postings: Exposure to different regions, customer segments, and banking verticals early in your career.

● Clear Promotion Ladder: A structured path from probationary officer up to general manager over the course of a career.

● Respect & Social Standing: A banking officer role continues to carry significant credibility, especially for families in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.

IBPS PO 2026 Highlights

Here is what has changed and what stands out in this year’s notification:

What’s New in IBPS PO 2026?

  • 6,715 vacancies were announced, around 1,507 more than the previous cycle.
  • A short application correction window has been introduced after registration closes.
  • The Mains exam now has 170 objective questions (up from 145 earlier).
  • Banking Awareness and Data Analysis & Interpretation sections carry higher weightage.
  • The English Language section has fewer marks and a shorter duration in Mains.
  • All other eligibility criteria and the three-stage selection process remain unchanged

IBPS PO Eligibility Criteria

Before applying, make sure you meet every eligibility parameter below. Any mismatch can lead to rejection at a later stage, even after clearing the exam.

Educational Qualification

Candidates need a bachelor’s degree in any discipline from a recognised university or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Government of India. You must hold a valid mark sheet or degree certificate confirming your graduate status on the date of registration, and you will need to enter your graduation percentage while filling the form.

Age Limit

Candidates must be a minimum of 20 years and a maximum of 30 years old as of 1st July 2026 — meaning you should be born between 2nd July 1996 and 1st July 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Age Relaxation

CategoryAge RelaxationSC / ST5 yearsOBC (Non-Creamy Layer)3 yearsPersons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)10 yearsEx-Servicemen5 yearsPersons affected by the 1984 riots5 yearsWidows / Divorced Women (not remarried)9 yearsJ&K Domicile (1.1.1980 – 31.12.1989)5 yearsUnion Carbide Factory (Bhopal) retrenched employees (MP only)5 years

Nationality

You are eligible to apply for IBPS PO 2026 if you are one of the following:

● A citizen of India, OR

● A subject of Nepal or Bhutan, OR

● A Tibetan refugee who settled permanently in India before 1st January 1962, OR

● A person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Burma (Myanmar), Vietnam, or East African countries such as Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, or Ethiopia, with the intention of settling permanently in India.

Candidates falling in the second, third, or fourth category must possess an eligibility certificate issued by the Government of India.

Computer Literacy Requirement

Since the entire selection process from the application form to the online exam is technology-driven, candidates are expected to have basic working knowledge of computer systems. This is also essential for day-to-day banking operations once you join as a probationary officer.

IBPS PO Application Fee

CategoryApplication Fee (Incl. GST)SC / ST / PwBDRs. 175/-General / EWS / OBCRs. 850/-

The fee must be paid entirely online through debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI at the time of application submission. Once paid, the fee is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other exam or cycle.

How to Apply Online

The complete IBPS PO 2026 application process is online-only through www.ibps.in. Follow these steps

carefully to avoid errors:

  1. Visit the official IBPS website and open the CRP PO/MT-XVI recruitment link.
  2. Click ‘New Registration’ and enter your name, contact details, and email ID to generate a provisional registration number and password.
  3. Save your registration number and password securely for future logins.
  4. Log back in and complete the application form with personal, educational, and communication details.
  5. Upload your scanned photograph, signature, and the IBPS PO handwritten declaration as per the prescribed specifications.
  6. Select your preferred exam centre and state cadre preferences where applicable.
  7. Carefully review every entry on the preview page before final submission.
  8. Pay the applicable application fee through the available online payment modes.
  9. Submit the form and download the confirmation page and fee receipt.
  10. Keep a printed copy of your final application for future reference.

Documents Required

● Recent passport-size photograph in the prescribed dimensions

● Scanned signature

● IBPS PO handwritten declaration in the specified format

● Graduation mark sheet and degree certificate

● Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), where applicable

● PwBD certificate, where applicable

● Valid photo ID proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, or Passport)

● A valid, active email ID for all official communication

IBPS PO Selection Process

Selection for the probationary officer post is a three-stage process: preliminary examination, main examination, and interview. Each stage is a filter; you must clear the sectional and overall cut-off at every stage to advance to the next.

StageNaturePurposePreliminary ExaminationQualifying (marks not counted in final merit)Shortlists candidates for the main examination.Main ExaminationScoring (Objective + Descriptive)Determines the pool of candidates called for an interviewInterviewScoring (Personality Test)Assesses overall suitability for an officer role

IBPS PO Prelims Exam Pattern

The Prelims are an online, qualifying-stage exam consisting of 100 questions for 100 marks in 60 minutes, with sectional timing of 20 minutes per section. A negative marking of 0.25 marks applies for every wrong answer.

SectionQuestionsMarksDurationEnglish Language303020 MinutesQuantitative Aptitude353020 MinutesReasoning Ability354020 MinutesTotal10010060 Minutes

IBPS PO Mains Exam Pattern (Latest Revised)

IBPS has revised the Mains pattern this year, increasing the total question count from 145 to 170 questions for 200 marks. General/Economy/Banking Awareness and Data Analysis & Interpretation now carry greater weightage, while the English Language section has fewer marks and a shorter duration.

SectionQuestionsMarksDurationReasoning406045 MinutesGeneral / Economy / Banking / Digital & Financial Awareness (incl. RBI Circulars)506035 MinutesEnglish Language402035 MinutesData Analysis & Interpretation406045 MinutesTotal170200160 Minutes

In addition to the objective paper, candidates attempt a descriptive test worth 25 marks (essay and comprehension with 2 questions in 30 minutes), conducted along with the main examination.

Interview Process

Candidates who clear the Mains cut-off are called for a personal interview worth 100 marks, typically lasting 15–20 minutes. A panel of bank officials assesses your communication skills, banking awareness, current affairs knowledge, and overall personality. The minimum qualifying mark is 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates).

Final Merit Calculation

The final selection is based purely on your combined mains and interview performance. Here is how it works:

● Prelims marks are NOT carried forward — they are only used to shortlist candidates for mains.

● You must individually clear both the Mains cut-off and the interview cut-off.

● Mains and interview marks are combined in an 80:20 weightage ratio.

● The combined score out of 100 is used to prepare the final category-wise merit list.

● Provisional bank allotment follows the final merit list, based on your preferences and available

vacancies.

IBPS PO Syllabus

The IBPS PO syllabus is broadly divided into the sections tested at Prelims and the additional sections that appear only in Mains.

English Language

Reading comprehension, cloze tests, para jumbles, error spotting, fill-in-the-blanks, sentence improvement, and paragraph completion.

Reasoning

Seating Arrangement, Puzzles, Syllogism, Blood Relations, Coding-Decoding, Input-Output, Data Sufficiency, Coded Inequalities, and Alphanumeric Series.

Quantitative Aptitude

Simplification, Number Series, Data Interpretation, Ratio & Proportion, Percentage, Profit & Loss, Simple & Compound Interest, Time & Work, Time & Distance, and Mensuration.

Data Analysis

Tabular, bar, line, and caselet-based data interpretation, along with data sufficiency and probability-based analytical questions this section carries increased weightage in the revised Mains pattern.


Banking Awareness

Current Affairs, Banking Terms, Monetary Policy, RBI Circulars and Guidelines, Government Schemes, Financial Institutions, and Static GK related to the banking and financial sector.


Descriptive Test

Essay writing on banking, economic, or social topics and a letter-writing or comprehension-based question — this component tests your written communication skills in English.

IBPS PO Salary 2026

The initial in-hand salary for an IBPS probationary officer ranges between Rs 74,000 and Rs 76,000 per month, inclusive of dearness allowance and other perks. The basic pay scale is fixed as per the latest revision applicable to Scale I officers.

In-Hand SalaryRs. 74,000 – Rs. 76,000 per monthDearness Allowance (DA)As per applicable bank rulesHouse Rent Allowance (HRA)As applicable to posting locationCity Compensatory Allowance (CCA)As applicableOther BenefitsMedical Benefits, LTC, Newspaper Allowance, Pension & other admissible perks

Allowances

Apart from the basic pay, probationary officers receive a dearness allowance, house rent allowance, city compensatory allowance, medical benefits, a leave travel concession, and a pension/provident fund benefit, making the overall compensation package considerably higher than the basic pay alone.

Career Growth


IBPS PO offers one of the clearest promotion ladders in Indian public sector banking:

● Probationary Officer (PO)

● Manager

● Senior Manager

● Assistant General Manager

● Deputy General Manager

● General Manager (TEGS-VII)

Promotions depend on tenure, internal examinations, and performance appraisals, but a motivated officer

can realistically reach senior management positions within 15–20 years of service.

Participating Banks

The following 11 public sector banks are participating in IBPS PO recruitment 2026:

● Bank of Baroda

● Bank of India

● Bank of Maharashtra

● Canara Bank

● Central Bank of India

● Indian Bank

● Indian Overseas Bank

● Punjab National Bank

● Punjab & Sind Bank

● UCO Bank

● Union Bank of India


Preparation Strategy

A well-structured strategy matters more than the number of hours you put in. Focus on accuracy first, then build speed through consistent mock test practice.

Best Books

● Quantitative Aptitude: A standard aptitude book covering Simplification, DI, and Arithmetic

fundamentals, supplemented with topic-wise practice sets.

● Reasoning Ability: A puzzle-and-seating-arrangement-focused practice book, since this topic

dominates both prelims and mains.

● English Language: A grammar and vocabulary-building book alongside daily reading comprehension practice from editorials.

● Banking & General Awareness: A monthly current affairs digest combined with a static banking

awareness handbook.

● Previous Year Papers: Solve at least the last 5 years of IBPS PO Prelims and Mains papers to

understand recurring question patterns.

90-Day Preparation Plan


● Days 1–30 (Foundation): Cover complete Reasoning, Quant, and English syllabus topic by topic. Start a daily banking awareness reading habit.

● Days 31–60 (Practice & Prelims Focus): Attempt sectional tests daily and begin weekly full-length

Do prelims mock tests and revise weak topics identified from mock analysis.

● Days 61–80 (Mains Preparation): Shift focus to data analysis & interpretation and banking/digital awareness. Begin practising the descriptive test format.

● Days 81–90 (Final Revision): Take full-length Mains mock tests, revise formulas and current affairs notes, and work exclusively on accuracy and time management.

Time Management Tips


● Attempt your strongest section first in every mock test to build early confidence and banked time.

● Set a strict per-question time cap during practice so you develop the instinct to skip and move on.

● Solve Data Interpretation sets before individual questions, since sets typically offer more marks per minute.

● Reserve the last 5 minutes of every section to review marked questions rather than attempting new ones.

● Track your section-wise accuracy weekly and adjust your practice ratio based on the results.


Common Mistakes to Avoid

● Filling the application form at the last minute and risking payment or server failures.

● Ignoring sectional cut-offs while chasing a high overall score.

● Ignoring banking and digital awareness until the last few weeks before mains.

● Skipping the descriptive test practice, which many candidates underestimate.

● Not analysing mock test mistakes properly before moving to the next test.

● Neglecting interview preparation until after the Mains result is declared.

How Do I Begin My IAS Preparation?

If you’re reading this, you’re probably among the many IAS hopefuls who want to work for this nation as a proud public servant but aren’t sure exactly how to get there.

We recognise your concern, and let us assure you that it is perfectly normal to be unsure about where to begin your IAS preparation. You undoubtedly have a hundred queries, ranging from when to start studying for one of the hardest exams to how to ace the personal interview.

This article will walk you through the best IAS preparation strategy from start to finish!

We must first learn more about the fundamentals of this exam in order to fully understand the preparation requirements for your exam.

How to Start IAS Preparation?

The following are some of the most crucial things to remember if you want to have your path featured in IAS success tales.

An Essential Component of the IAS Preparation Strategy is Understanding the Exam Pattern.

There are three sections to the curriculum heavy exam paper.

  • The Prelims
  • The Mains
  • The Interview

Without passing the previous step, you cannot move on to the next.

Each step will be more difficult than the one before.

The candidate must possess a solid understanding of a wide range of subjects for the first two rounds.

During the first two levels, the student is expected to demonstrate their conceptual and diagnostic abilities in a condensed amount of time.

Even while the final round, also known as the personal interview round, does not assess your writing skills, it still necessitates the same level of awareness and expertise as the earlier phases.

Keep track of the dates and syllabus.

Your ability to adhere as closely as possible to UPSC syllabus as whowell as the scheduled exam dates will determine how successful you are.

The timing of the exam will typically be as follows:

  • June for Preliminaries
  • September/October for mains
  • April to February for interview

Preliminary exam dates are moved up in 2021 as a result of the nationwide shutdown and Corona Virus epidemic.

Not to terrify you, but the syllabus is quite extensive. Start your preparations at least a year before your exam date, according to experts.

Analyse the competition with reality.

It also serves as one of the main qualifying tests in the nation in addition to being the hardest exam. Like you, thousands of candidates are competing for the prestigious job of an Indian civil servant.

I’ll give you a rough idea of the scenario for this important exam:

Since 49.5% of the seats are reserved, it’s possible that if you fall under the general category, you’ll need to get into the top 50% to make the final rank list.

How to prepare for competitive exams?

Are you planning to take a competitive entrance exam? Concerned about how to prepare for competitive exams. We recognise that you may be working very hard to pass these tests. However, sometimes when preparing, we tend to take things for granted and overlook some of the crucial details that may later prove to be obstacles. Competitive entrance examinations are difficult, but not impossible. You can pass the examinations if you put in the necessary amount of smart study and dedication. To pass these exams, you will need to hone a few talents. 

Millions of students take difficult competitive entrance tests each year to pursue a higher education or careers. Competitive Exam preparation is the first thought that comes to mind. It is difficult to pass any admission exam in today’s competitive environment because there are only a limited number of seats available. Thousands of students take the exam in order to obtain those seats, and only a few are chosen based on their qualifications and performance. As you are aware, competitive exams can be challenging for students because they must cover a large portion of the course. This may cause anxiousness and even tension when preparing.

Previously, students were rarely provided with enough facilities for competitive exam preparation, but advances in technology and the internet have alleviated this challenge to a greater extent. Students nowadays strive to do their best in order to get selected and progress toward their goals. And if you are one of the students taking the entrance exam, make sure to use the tips to prepare for competitive exams. Even the simplest tips and tricks can help you prepare for the exam better. Let’s look at 10 tips and tricks for how to prepare for competitive exams so you can ace those difficult admission tests.

How to prepare for competitive exams tips and tricks

1 Understand and read about the exam.

Understanding the competitive exam that you’re applying for is the first step. As each competitive exam is unique from others, it is crucial to thoroughly read the instructions and application process before submitting your application. You should be aware of the purpose of the test and how passing it would benefit your career. If you intend to prepare for the IAS, follow all procedures and create an IAS preparation plan.

2 Set Up Your Study Area

Do you have a home study space? If not, choose a more quiet place for your study session. Make sure to arrange the things you need for a better study environment, such as a cosy chair and a table, light, stationery, books, etc., in accordance with your preferences.. Everything must be set up to your liking so that you can learn with absolute concentration and enthusiasm. A tidy environment promotes optimism and personality.

3 Analyse the Syllabus

Explore and analyse the syllabus given in the application before beginning to prepare for the competitive exam. You should be aware of the syllabus and subject matter that must be studied for the exam. Organise your course material into chapters and modules. Before beginning your preparation, you should review the syllabus. Also, examine the marks assigned to each section of the syllabus. Then, according to the weightage of the syllabus, you can begin prioritising your studies for the exam.

4 Create a Timetable

Before you begin studying and practising for the competitive exam, plan and set a timetable. You can incorporate the syllabus on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis until the tests are completed. Set up a day and a time for every unit to learn and practise on a daily basis, along with any necessary brief breaks. Everyone is aware that sticking to a schedule increases one’s discipline and sincerity toward their studies and their environment. Make sure that you establish realistic goals for the exam as you create your study schedule, and organise the hours for when you feel most motivated and productive in your academic pursuits.

The plan should be simple and clear to understand when you look at it. For complex information, allot more time than for basic information. In order to finish studying, make sure to closely stick to the timeframe and chapter goals for the day.

5 Get Rid of Distractions

You may become distracted by minor details while preparing. In order to prepare, you must concentrate on grasping the syllabus and the topics. Many papers are largely analytical questions. In order to improve your learning outcomes, you should concentrate on understanding them. Remembering information is way easier if you are attentive and sincere. To concentrate more on passing the exam, it’s vital to remove any outside distractions. Distractions can include excessive mobile phone use, prolonged chat sessions, game playing, etc. In order to effectively prepare for the exam, it is crucial to maintain focus.

6 Adopting a Healthier Lifestyle

The most crucial aspect of existence is health. You can only attain your goals if your mental and physical health are in good shape. Make sure you get a sufficient amount of sleep each night when studying because sleep deprivation can lead to fatigue and have a poor effect on exams. The key to maintaining a happy outlook is to plan a consistent routine. You should consume plenty of water, maintain a nutritious diet, and exercise frequently. Daily exercise as well as meditation can promote better focus levels while learning. Make certain that you are not being pressured or sidetracked by anyone. Taking regular breaks throughout preparation is essential for both the mind and the body. Use the additional time for rest and meditation.

7 Stay Motivated

To pass the exam, you must have motivation and confidence. You can accomplish your goals if you have faith in yourself and keep yourself motivated. Continue to believe in your ability to pass the test and be chosen. You need to surround yourself with people who can inspire and encourage you while you’re preparing. Don’t worry as much about the outcome; instead, give your all throughout the preparation.

#8 Drill / Practise

Previous test papers might make a significant impact in your preparation. When exam papers are delivered, it’s common to have a hard time understanding the questions because they appear so distinct and complex. You can gain insight in these situations by going back and reviewing the question papers from the prior year. It can help in knowing the types of questions that may be asked on the exam. Therefore, gather question papers from the previous five decades and try to study since you never know when a question from one of those papers will come up in the exam. It will also offer you a general notion of the issues that should be given top importance. For better preparation, there are numerous online platforms that allow you to practise exams.

9 Managing Your Time

The most crucial tip you can start using right now is to manage your time. Understanding how to manage your time will make passing these tests stress- and anxiety-free. Time management includes not only preparation but also the amount of time you allot to each exam question. There are many online test-taking resources that can aid you with practice, test-taking techniques, and time management skills for better preparation.

10 Seek guidance

If you have any questions or concerns about the exam, do not be afraid to ask for help. Sometimes you may consider working hard to obtain the proper information or notions, but this may result in a waste of time. Instead, you can talk to your professors or friends about your concerns.

UPSC Civil Services Exam 2023 Syllabus

The UPSC Civil Services Examination is drawing the young generation. Following the Covid era, an increasing number of individuals began to apply for and take this exam.

Everyone should be familiar with the UPSC IAS Syllabus 2023 before entering this intense competition.

  • First read through the UPSC IAS Exam Syllabus.
  • Plan and gather the best study materials for the UPSC preliminary and main exams.
  • Plan how you will finish this syllabus in a certain amount of time. Revision is key, so do it often.

Stage 1: Preliminary UPSC exam

There are two sections to the preliminary examination:

a) General Studies

PaperSubjectsTotal MarksDurationIGeneral Studies(GS)2002 hours (9:30 AMto 11:30 AM)IICSAT2002 hours (2:30 PM to4:30 PM)

b ) Civil Services Aptitude Test (CSAT)

  • Generally speaking, the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination comprises two objective-type papers, each worth 200 points (for a total of 400 points), and lasting two hours. An applicant must attempt both exams in order to be eligible for the Civil Services Mains.
  • Additionally, the CSAT paper has 80 questions, whereas the UPSC General Studies (GS) paper has 100 questions. For incorrect responses, 1/3 of the total points for that question are deducted from the final score for both papers.
  • This is further demonstrated by the fact that each well solved GS question will receive two points. The total would be reduced by 0.66 marks for each question that was marked incorrectly.
  • Similar to the CSAT paper, which consists of 80 questions worth 200 total points, each correctly answered CSAT question is worth 2.5 points, while incorrectly marked questions result in a penalty of 0.833 points per incorrect response, which will be subtracted from the final score.
  • No marks will be deducted for questions that have not been attempted.

The two IAS preliminary exams papers are covered in detail below:

  1. General Studies (Typically carried out between 9:30 am and 11:30 am)

The preliminary examination’s first paper is the General Studies test. This exam is designed to evaluate a candidate’s general knowledge of a variety of topics, including Indian politics, geography, history, economics, technology and science, the environment and ecology, international relations, and related UPSC current affairs.

  1. CSAT: Civil Services Aptitude Test (Generally conducted between 2:30 PM to 04:30 PM)
  • In addition to “Reading Comprehension” and the occasional “Decision Making” questions, this UPSC Prelims syllabus for CSAT aims to evaluate the candidate’s capacity for handling “Reasoning and Analytical” problems.
  • Negative marks are typically not applied to questions that are based on “Decision Making.”
  • Only candidates who pass the preliminary exam will advance to the other levels of the test.
  • The Prelims marks will not be added for calculating the final rank list.

UPSC IAS Syllabus 2023 Civil Services Syllabus for Prelims

Syllabus for the GS Exam (Prelims Paper I)

  • important current events on a national and international level.
  • Indian history and the Indian National Movement
  • Physical, social, and economic geography of India and the rest of the world.
  • Constitution, political system, panchayati raj, public policy, rights issues, etc. of Indian politics and governance.
  • Economic and social development – poverty, inclusion, demographics, social sector efforts, etc.
  • Climate change, biodiversity, and environmental ecology are all general topics that don’t require subject specialisation.
  • Basic Science

Syllabus for the CSAT Exam (Prelims Paper II)

  • Comprehension
  • Interpersonal abilities, particularly communication abilities
  • logical thinking and reasoning
  • Making decisions and solving problems
  • general cognitive capacity
  • Simple mathematics (numbers and their relations, orders of magnitude, etc.) (Class X level), interpretation of data (charts, graphs, tables, data sufficiency etc. – Class X level)

Stage 2: UPSC Mains Exam (1750 Marks)

  • The second phase of the Civil Services Exam is the Mains examination. Candidates wouldn’t be able to take the IAS Mains until they had successfully passed the prelims exam.
  • The Mains exam examines a candidate’s depth of academic competence and speed at which he or she can articulate their understanding in response to a question’s criteria.
  • Nine papers make up the UPSC Mains exam, of which two are qualifying papers at 300 points each.
  • The following are the two qualifying papers:
  1. Any Indian Language
  2. English Language Paper

Only those candidates’ essay, general studies, and optional subject papers that meet the minimum qualifying threshold of 25% on both language exams will be taken into consideration for review.

The marks a candidate receives will not be taken into account or counted if they fail to pass these language papers.

Structure of the language papers:

The types of questions asked are –

  • Essay – 100 marks
  • Reading comprehension – 60 marks
  • Precis Writing – 60 marks
  • Translation:
  • English to compulsory language (e.g. Hindi) – 20 marks
  • Compulsory language to English – 20 marks
  • Grammar and basic language usage – 40 marks
  • The rest of the seven papers can be written in any of the languages mentioned under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India or in English.

Stage 3: IAS Interview/UPSC Personality Test (275 Marks)

  • The “Personality Test/Interview” is required of candidates who pass the UPSC Mains Exam. A Board chosen by the UPSC will interview these candidates.
  • Typically, there are more than three times as many applicants summoned for the personality test as there are open positions within a given year.
  • The goal of the interview is for a panel of knowledgeable and objective observers to evaluate the candidate’s overall suitability for a job in the civil services.
  • The purpose of the interview is to learn more about the applicant’s mental capabilities and analytical skills.
  • The written examination will have a maximum score of 1750 points, and the interview will be worth 275 points. This adds up to a Grand Total of 2025 Marks, which will serve as the foundation for creating the final merit list.

Here are Subject-Wise CLAT Preparation Tips 2023.

To excel in the upcoming exam, try paying attention to these suggestions and improving your level of preparation.

How Can I Prepare for the CLAT 2023 English Exam?

  • Similar to the adage “Rome wasn’t built in a day,” learning the English language takes time and requires a significant amount of reading to become proficient.
  • To prepare for the CLAT in English, read the editorials and opinion columns in the newspaper.
  • It is possible to enhance your English by reading newspapers articles and discussion columns.

Improve Your Grammar

  • You must learn the fundamentals of grammar, which you can do even with grammar textbooks for elementary school.
  • To get a good score on CLAT 2023, you must, however, improve your grammar and spelling errors.

Thorough Reading

  • To get better at language, read more. To improve your vocabulary, read books, periodicals, newspapers, and novels.
  • You must prepare thoroughly for CLAT English, particularly Comprehension, if you want to perform well on the English section.

Here are CLAT Preparation Tips 2023 for Math Section?

Since the questions are intended to test you on simple mathematics, or the fundamental arithmetic you learnt until class 10, mathematics might not be a significant concern for law aspirants.

Consequently, you can quickly earn points in this part. You will, however, need to practise on a regular basis.

To improve your preparation, use the CLAT 2023 Maths Preparation Tips listed below.

  • Regularly commit to memory squares and tables up to 20.
  • It is sufficient to read the NCERT Mathematics textbooks for classes 9 and 10.
  • Know the pertinent subjects and comprehend each idea completely.
  • So, unwind. Go back and review some of your schoolbooks.

How to Prepare for CLAT 2023 Legal Aptitude Section?

Legal aptitude continues to be the most crucial section of CLAT 2023. The questions in the legal aptitude section are designed to test your problem-solving ability in legal issues.

You can apply a time management strategy while solving legal aptitude questions based on legal matters, public policies, and moral philosophies.

CLAT Preparation Tips 2023 can help you prepare better for the CLAT Legal Aptitude exam.

  • The Legal Penal Code and the Indian Constitution are important books to consult for this.
  • Consult publications like “Legal Glossary Terms” and “Most Commonly Used Legal Terms.”
  • By reading the news as well as watching the news, you can expand your vocabulary for the law.
  • It is also beneficial to read legal publications in order to gain a much more legal perspective on problems or a more legal view on important matters.

How to Prepare for CLAT 2023 Logical Reasoning?

  • Understand the fundamentals of the topics covered in the syllabus and make sure your notions are clear.
  • Concentrate more on ancestry, directions, numerical sequences, drawing inferences, etc.
  • Study and resolve verbal and nonverbal reasoning problems.
  • Try to answer as many questions from last year’s exams as you can.
  • Try your best every day to tackle logic-based puzzles and games.

How to Prepare for CLAT 2023 Current affairs and General Knowledge?

  • Basic familiarity with history, geography, & science will be highly valued.
  • Making a daily habit of reading the newspaper is one of the best CLAT Preparation Tips.
  • Do not pack occasions or dates. Instead, investigate why something occurred. Get an understanding of these issues.
  • Write down key dates, honours, and other information in your notes. This will be useful when you are studying.
  • Considerable newspapers and periodicals are your best bets for current affairs.

content:
